source_en: Back from the water lines. Prayers next.
Returning to the seminary house.
Delivering donated blankets to the sector.
Counseling at the triage center.
Running the basement soup kitchen.
Checking on parish families before curfew.
Last rites. No one should die alone.
Back into the smog with kind words.
To the cathedral. Bells cracked, not silent.
Opening my new bar tonight.
Back from a lucky night at the casino.
Collecting a shipment of imported caviar.
Closing the soup kitchen. Not my concern.
Staying home. I avoid the sick.
Off to my dacha until it passes.
Leaving the dying to others. I need rest.
Locking the cathedral doors for good.
Staying in. I avoid people now.
Hello, brother! A grim morning, but we're still here, aren't we?
My papers. I've been out since dawn on the water lines.
The ash gets into everything, even the pews. My application.
People need more than bread now. They need a reason to smile.
Back into the smog. People are scared and alone out there.
The bells are cracked, but the message holds. We're not abandoned.
God bless your work today. Stay strong!
Chin up. I'll mention you in my thoughts tonight.
Whatever comes, you did your duty. Peace be with you.
Then let this be my cell and my ministry both.
Whatever I carry, let it stay here, away from the others.
Carry this gently… It is a heavy thing…
Lord… receive me… I tried to do enough…
Where are you coming from?
The east district water lines since dawn, brother. Then evening prayers.
The cathedral soup kitchen, then the triage center. So many frightened people.
The streets. Three last rites today. Someone must sit with them.
My mountain monastery. I live alone up there. I rarely come down.
The district committee records office. The collar is only for Sundays.
The rectory. Twenty years alone there. There were never any brothers.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
The spirit is willing, brother. The body is only tired. Nothing more.
A small tremor in my left hand. I hide it at the altar.
I am always warm, even at night. No time to ask why.
None. I have not left my bed in days. Rest was all I needed.
Nothing. I am not yet thirty. The body keeps up with the work.
Nothing. I stayed inside the cathedral all week. Nowhere near the sick.
You look tired, officer. I'll mention you in my prayers tonight.
Someone has to hold the line. I'm glad it's someone like you.
We keep the cathedral doors open, ash or no ash.
A dozen more families to check on before curfew. Pray for my feet.
Let us finish this chapter, brother, and see the next page.
There are people alone in the smog who need a voice.
